key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning outperformed the multitask neural network for all three welding targets, with the largest gains in ultimate tensile strength (UTS) prediction.
engineering_relevance: Predicting UTS, weld hardness, and heat-affected zone (HAZ) hardness can support welding process optimization and assessment of joint performance.
method: Train a multitask neural network with shared hidden layers and task-specific outputs.
Compare against stacking ensemble learning on a shared welding dataset.
Evaluate each target using RMSE and R².
evidence_signal: Stacking versus multitask R² was 0.9863 vs 0.6724 for UTS, 0.9782 vs 0.9215 for weld hardness, and 0.8453 vs 0.8407 for HAZ hardness.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset size, validation design, or RMSE scaling, limiting assessment of generalization and practical error magnitude.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
